text: Increase SQLite busy_timeout to 30s for MCP server processes. Current 5s timeout in connection.go is too short when multiple processes contend on backlogit.db write lock. Effort: trivial. Impact: high.

Add write-retry wrapper with exponential backoff for SQLite operations. Wrap all DB write operations with a retry helper that catches SQLITE_BUSY errors and retries (3 retries: 1s/2s/4s backoff). No retry logic exists anywhere currently. Effort: moderate. Impact: high.

Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write transactions in SQLite. Rehydrate, UpsertItem, and other write paths currently use default deferred transactions, which only acquire the write lock at first write statement. This means lock conflicts are detected late (at commit or mid-transaction), wasting work that gets rolled back. BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the lock at transaction start, failing fast and enabling retry at the boundary. Effort: moderate -- add sql.TxOptions to BeginTx calls in rehydration.go, queries.go, etc. Impact: moderate -- prevents wasted work under contention.

Break Rehydrate into smaller batched transactions. Currently Rehydrate() in rehydration.go holds a single write transaction for the entire DELETE-all + filesystem-walk + rebuild cycle. On large workspaces this holds the SQLite write lock for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, blocking all other writers. Restructure to commit in batches (e.g., N items per transaction) to reduce maximum lock hold time. Effort: moderate -- restructure rehydration loop with batch commits while preserving atomicity guarantees. Impact: moderate -- reduces max contention window during sync operations.
Internal lifecycle hooks for validation, cascade, and enforcement
External system hooks with prioritized notification push support for Slack, Teams, and webhooks

Add a stash.jsonl file to .backlogit/archive/ that collects each stash entry as it is staged and pulled into a shipment after deliberation. This preserves a durable record of all prior stash entries, including their original text, priority, kind, linked deliberation ID, and the harvested artifact ID. Currently, removed stash entries disappear entirely from stash.jsonl with no historical trace.

Add stash hygiene to the Stage workflow. Stage agent guidance still lacks a standard stale-stash pruning step even though stash entries now expose `age_days` and support `stash remove` and `stash edit`; update the agent protocol and refresh the stale compound doc so future agents stop falling back to raw `stash.jsonl` edits.
backlogit needs a --version flag to allow users to determine which version they are running on from the CLI and perhaps also as an MCP command.

Need a way to format output of queue and stash items in a tabular format and also in a tile-like format like a quote section with Property: Value combinations. This will allow for better CLI output and readability as well as enabling better output for messaging systems like agent-intercom where we would push out a single message for each queue or stash item for messaging purposes when I want to know what's still in the stash or queue.
Change documentation structure to reduce size of ReadMe file

Write compound doc: ship-agent post-merge closure must archive source deliberations and stash entries, not just the items it implemented. Root cause: shipments are closing without back-tracing to their source artifacts (the deliberation that defined the work and the stash entry that originated it). Evidence from 2026-04-19 stage session — three stale-scope sweeps in one session: (1) 033-DL Event Traceability deliberation queued after 006-S shipped its scope; (2) 031-DL Telemetry Pipeline Enhancements deliberation queued after commit 24487b8 shipped its scope (note: archived shipment 031-S has misleading title — says "Telemetry Pipeline Enhancements" but custom_fields.items lists SQLite reliability items 031-F + 031.001..004-T, so title alone is unreliable for shipment audit); (3) 034-DL Stash Archive + 035-DL Stash Hygiene deliberations + stash entries 46CC1C9D + A8F688A7 all queued after shipment 014-S shipped on 2026-04-12. Recommended action: add a post-merge closure step to ship.agent.md (or operational-closure skill) that follows source links from shipped feature/task back to the originating deliberation and stash entry, archives the deliberation via backlogit_archive_item, and removes the stash entry via backlogit_stash_remove with reason "superseded by {shipment_id}". Compound doc target: docs/compound/workflow-issues/ship-agent-source-artifact-archival-pattern-2026-04-19.md following existing template format (see ship-agent-incomplete-git-staging-pr-bypass-2026-04-14.md for structure).

When AdoptItem rewrites an artifact's ID and renames its file, other artifacts whose frontmatter references the old ID (e.g. parent_id, dependencies) are not updated. Stale edges reappear on next rehydration. Need a cross-artifact frontmatter reference rewrite step in AdoptItem that scans all artifacts for references to the old ID and updates them atomically.

Deliberate MCP merge sync for .backlogit drift detection with targeted cache updates, narrow stash/log rebuilds, and safe full-rehydrate fallback. Context: docs/memory/20260420-merge-sync-mcp-deliberation-context.md
Make the backlogit binary a releasable, stand-alone executable that doesn't need to be installed using golang and doesn't need golang installed on the machine to work.

Need to test the usage and context window log scraper.  Need to test the functionality and identify actual results. Start working on metrics and possibly a markdown report builder, although graphics would be a challenge with this approach.

Hook event queue writes are not crash-durable. internal/events/hook_events.go appends to .backlogit/hooks_queue.jsonl and returns success without fsync or equivalent durability step after the write. A power loss or OS crash can lose the just-assigned event after sequence allocation, which risks missed hook notifications or duplicate/replayed sequence handling on recovery. Fix by making queue appends durably committed before returning success and add regression coverage for crash-safe hook queue persistence.

Hook consumer checkpoint writes are not crash-durable. internal/events/hook_checkpoint.go writes the temp checkpoint file with os.WriteFile and renames it into place without syncing the file contents first. After a crash, the checkpoint can regress or be corrupted, causing hook consumers to replay already-processed events from seq 0. Fix by writing checkpoint temp files through an explicit file handle, syncing before rename, and adding durability-focused tests for restart/replay behavior.

Telemetry JSONL harvest output is not crash-durable. internal/telemetry/harvest.go writes .backlogit/telemetry-sessions.jsonl through a temp file and rename, but never syncs the temp file before closing and renaming it. A crash can leave telemetry harvest results truncated or lost even though harvest reported success. Fix by syncing the temp file before close/rename and add regression coverage for durable telemetry record persistence.

Hook queue stale-lock recovery has a race window that can permit corrupted concurrent writes. internal/events/hook_events.go checks a stale .lock sidecar, removes it, and then retries lock acquisition, which creates a TOCTOU gap between stat/remove/reopen across processes. Two writers can race through stale-lock cleanup and both proceed against hooks_queue.jsonl. Fix by making stale-lock recovery atomic or replacing the sidecar pattern with a stronger cross-process lock primitive, and add concurrent writer regression coverage.

The CLI delete command can orphan artifact files if filesystem deletion fails. internal/cli/delete.go deletes the item from the SQLite index first and only then removes the markdown file from disk. If os.Remove fails after DeleteItemCascade succeeds, the artifact file remains in the workspace but is no longer tracked in the index, creating filesystem/index divergence that backlogit cannot manage cleanly. Fix by making delete ordering crash-safe and consistency-safe, with regression coverage for file-delete failures.

Stash harvest can commit stash removal before ensuring the new artifact is indexed. In internal/core/stash.go, harvestStashEntryLocked creates the artifact file, rewrites stash.jsonl to remove the source entry, and only then calls db.UpsertItem for the harvested artifact. If UpsertItem fails, the stash entry is already gone and the artifact file exists on disk but is missing from the index, leaving the workspace inconsistent. Fix by making harvest atomic across stash rewrite and artifact indexing, or by restoring stash/file state on index failure, with regression coverage for UpsertItem failures after stash rewrite.

ArchiveItem can leave file storage and the index out of sync when the post-move DB update fails. internal/core/archive.go writes the archived file, removes the original file, and only then updates the items table status to archived. If the database update fails, the file has already moved to archive but the index still reflects the old state, producing an inconsistent archive lifecycle. Fix by restoring file state on DB failure or restructuring the archive operation to preserve file/index consistency under partial failure.

Invalid semantic link types can enter the item_links index during rehydration and merge_sync. internal/models/frontmatter.go accepts any string for link_type, and internal/db/rehydration.go plus internal/db/merge_sync.go insert those values directly into item_links without using the validation enforced by internal/db/links.go AddLink. This allows malformed or unsupported link types in markdown frontmatter to be silently indexed, breaking data integrity and making link queries inconsistent with the supported domain. Fix by validating frontmatter link types before persistence and/or enforcing allowed values at the schema layer with regression coverage for invalid link_type inputs.

Manifest relocation detection depends on a lossy 512-byte frontmatter scan for item IDs. internal/db/manifest.go extractItemIDFromFrontmatter reads only the first 512 bytes and uses string-prefix matching instead of the normal frontmatter parser. Artifacts with large or unusual frontmatter can end up with an empty ItemID in the manifest, causing move/rename detection in merge_sync to degrade into delete-plus-add behavior instead of relocation. Fix by using the real frontmatter parser or a robust bounded YAML parse for manifest ID extraction, and add coverage for artifacts whose id field appears later in frontmatter.

Doctor orphan detection produces false positives for legacy top-level task and bug artifacts. internal/core/doctor.go decides child-ness from configured artifact type hierarchy alone, so archived items like 001-T and 001-B with level 1 / hierarchy_path 001 are reported as orphaned artifacts even though they are stored as top-level legacy items. This makes doctor output noisy and undermines integrity checks. Fix by basing orphan detection on the artifact's actual stored hierarchy level or legacy migration rules instead of type-level defaults alone.

The CLI is missing the doctor command even though backlogit exposes doctor through MCP and repository docs direct operators to run `backlogit doctor`. Running `go run ./cmd/backlogit doctor` currently fails with `unknown command \"doctor\"`, and there is no internal/cli doctor command wired into root.go. This breaks operator workflows described in docs and closure guidance. Fix by implementing/wiring the CLI doctor command (or removing the documented contract if it is intentionally unsupported) and add CLI coverage for the command surface.

Telemetry harvest does not parse current Copilot CLI log format. backlogit_telemetry_harvest records session metadata but all usage metrics stay at zero because the parser expects single-line [telemetry] cli.model_call / cli.tool_call JSON, while current .copilot logs emit multi-line [Telemetry] cli.telemetry / cli.restricted_telemetry records with nested kind, properties, and metrics fields. Fix by updating the telemetry parser and correlator to support the current log format, extract session/model/token/tool-call metrics correctly, preserve incremental harvest and since filtering behavior, and add regression tests using real current-format log fixtures so telemetry report/list/top return non-zero usage when logs contain usage data.

Need a way to implement disaster recovery of agent session ending suddenly, which can happen when using a remote server or if the power gets shut off.  This may involve a combination of agent harness improvements and backlogit tooling.  Need to perform adequate research and analysis to understand what this feature entails.

Plugin manifest and directory structure — Create `plugin.json` manifest and organize existing agents (.github/agents/*.agent.md), skills (.github/skills/*/SKILL.md), and MCP server config into plugin-compatible layout. Plugin must reference the npm wrapper package for MCP server binary resolution.

npm wrapper package (@backlogit/backlogit-mcp) — Create the main npm package with a hybrid binary resolver: (1) check PATH for native backlogit binary, (2) resolve from @backlogit/{platform}-{arch} optional dependencies, (3) fall back to downloading from GitHub Releases. Includes bin/backlogit-mcp entry point, install.js postinstall script, and package.json with optionalDependencies for all supported platforms.

Platform-specific npm packages — Create package.json templates for @backlogit/linux-x64, @backlogit/linux-arm64, @backlogit/darwin-x64, @backlogit/darwin-arm64, @backlogit/win32-x64 with os/cpu fields for npm platform filtering. Each package contains the pre-compiled Go binary for its platform.

Cross-compilation CI pipeline — GitHub Actions workflow that cross-compiles backlogit for all target platforms (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64) using Go GOOS/GOARCH, packages each binary into its platform-specific npm package, publishes all packages to npm, and uploads binaries to GitHub Releases.
Fix Copilot telemetry parser bufio.Scanner token-too-long handling so oversized log entries do not produce partial zero-token sessions
Fix telemetry top docs: command currently reports server-level tool-call counts, not top tool calls by token usage
Document telemetry harvest side effects: it rehydrates SQLite telemetry tables in addition to writing telemetry-sessions.jsonl
Document harvested telemetry fields and metrics: tokens_by_model, tool_calls_by_server, completed_tasks, tokens_per_task, and context-window metrics

Need full stash-kind support to align with configured work item types. Add spike as a first-class stash kind, and evaluate or enable other kinds that should be stageable directly from the stash: subtask, deliberation, review, and shipment. Ideally stash kinds are driven from configured work item metadata rather than a hardcoded list so stash intake stays consistent with backlog capabilities.

Add `--json` output support to each CLI command and add a `backlogit manifest` command. The `--json` output must use the expected JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and result/error shapes so an agent can consume CLI responses the same way it consumes backlogit's MCP server responses. The manifest command should emit a JSON-RPC manifest of backlogit CLI tool commands, with names and descriptions aligned with the MCP tools list returned during MCP initialization. Ensure the CLI command inventory and descriptions stay consistent across CLI manifest output and MCP tool discovery.

Spike follow-up: telemetry attribution analytics — per-tool token attribution design, session timestamps/compaction persistence, expand tool/server attribution for engram/graphtor/backlogit/builtin tools, define comparison views for token-efficiency trends over time. Depends on attribution fix from B4491F8C.

Telemetry attribution and analytics enhancement — fix per-server token attribution (currently map[string]string, should be map[string]int with proportional allocation), expand hardcoded attribution registry to support graphtor/newer MCP servers, add cross-session comparison and trending views for token-efficiency analysis, verify post-harvest data quality. Core JSONL datastore and incremental ingestion already complete from 046-F.

Copilot CLI plugin distribution for backlogit — hybrid npm wrapper with native binary fallback. Create a Copilot CLI plugin (`plugin.json`) that bundles backlogit's agents, skills, and MCP server config. Solve the binary distribution problem using the esbuild-style npm wrapper pattern with a hybrid resolver: (1) check for native `backlogit` in PATH first, (2) resolve from platform-specific npm optional dependencies, (3) fall back to downloading from GitHub Releases. This enables `copilot plugin install softwaresalt/backlogit` for zero-setup onboarding.
Release the next backlogit binary after the CLI/docs audit: resolve repo-wide gofmt -l . drift outside the change set, bump the version, and start the release build/deployment pipeline.
backlogit harvest doesn't seem to work; reports failed to parse session events, scan session events: bufio.Scanner: token too long.

Exclude zero-activity sessions from telemetry aggregations and averages. Sessions with TotalTokens==0 AND ModelCalls==0 AND ToolCalls==0 are ghost sessions (session initialized but no model interaction occurred) and skew averages significantly. These should be: (1) still shown in telemetry list with a visual indicator (e.g. dim/[empty] marker) so they are discoverable, but (2) excluded from all average calculations in telemetry trend and telemetry report, and (3) excluded from the session count used to compute AVG_TOKENS/SESSION and AVG_PEAK_UTIL in trend output. The 64-session harvest showed ~12 zero-activity sessions inflating the denominator.

Add model calls and tool calls columns to telemetry trend output. The TrendGroup struct currently only aggregates tokens, tokens-per-task, and peak utilization. Add AvgModelCalls and AvgToolCalls fields so operators can see call-rate trends over time alongside token trends. Both fields are available in SessionSummaryRecord but not aggregated in GenerateTrendReport.

Derive and capture model class from model name during telemetry harvest. Parse the model string (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4.6' -> class='sonnet', 'claude-haiku-4.5' -> class='haiku', 'claude-opus-4.7' -> class='opus', 'gpt-5.4' -> class='gpt', 'o3-mini' -> class='o3') and store a ModelClass field in SessionSummaryRecord. Expose model class as a group-by dimension in telemetry report (--by class) and as a column in telemetry trend, so operators can see token consumption and call rates broken down by model tier rather than exact version.

Surface model names per session in telemetry list and report views. TokensByModel map is already captured in SessionSummaryRecord but is never shown in the table output of telemetry list or telemetry report --by session. Add a PRIMARY_MODEL column showing the model with the highest token share for that session, and support a --by model group-by option in telemetry report to aggregate token and call counts by model name across all sessions.

Derive reasoning level from model name for OpenAI reasoning models during telemetry harvest. The cli.model_call payload does not include an explicit reasoning_level field; however, model names like 'o1', 'o3', 'o4-mini', 'o3-mini' imply reasoning. Map known OpenAI o-series model names to a ReasoningLevel string ('high' for o1/o3/o4, 'low' for o3-mini/o4-mini) stored in SessionSummaryRecord. For Anthropic models and other providers, leave ReasoningLevel empty. Scope is intentionally limited: this is a model-name-derived heuristic, not a field from the raw telemetry payload.

events.jsonl Fact Table Harvest — Add granular fact-table telemetry by parsing .copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl files. Produces two JSONL fact tables in .backlogit/telemetry/: tool-calls.jsonl (one row per tool call with name, server, session, branch, repo, model, duration, success) and session-facts.jsonl (one row per shutdown-event session with per-model token breakdown and context window breakdown). Adds --by tool and --by context reporting dimensions to backlogit telemetry report. Incremental checkpoint via HarvestCheckpoint.ProcessedEventSessions. Live harvest verified: 38,910 tool call facts across 60 sessions, 44 session facts. All quality gates pass. PR #98 open on feat/054-events-fact-harvest awaiting merge.

Cascading archive cleanup: backlogit tool should own data-integrity cascades so agent crashes don't leave artifact leftovers. (1) When a shipment archives, cascade archive to all child features/tasks/subtasks in its manifest. (2) When a feature archives with linked stash entries, mark those stash entries as archived in the stash index. (3) Add a 'backlogit doctor --fix-orphans' mode that detects and resolves orphaned queue items after shipment close. The agent harness retains ownership of workflow decisions (when to trigger transitions), but backlogit enforces referential consistency on every state transition.

Rename backlogit_stash_remove to backlogit_stash_archive with removal_reason 'archived' instead of 'removed'. The current 'remove' naming implies deletion but the operation is a soft-delete that archives to archive/stash.jsonl. Renaming to 'archive' better communicates intent and aligns with the archive pattern used elsewhere (backlogit_archive_item). Keep backward compatibility by accepting the old name as an alias during a deprecation period.

Include SQL schema in metadata catalog output. The backlogit_get_metadata_catalog tool returns workspace config, artifact types, templates, stash config, and MCP tool inventory but does not include the SQLite schema (table names, columns, types, indexes, FTS virtual tables). Agents using backlogit_query_sql must currently rely on instruction files for schema knowledge. Add a sql_schema section to the catalog response containing table definitions and column metadata so agents can construct correct queries without needing instruction file context. This also makes the tool surface self-describing for new agents that lack pre-loaded instructions.

Add 'backlogit telemetry schema' subcommand that prints a human-readable reference of all harvested telemetry data. For each fact table (tool-calls.jsonl, session-facts.jsonl, telemetry-sessions.jsonl), show: table name, friendly description, and a field listing with name, type, and brief description. Output formats: text (default), json, markdown. This helps operators understand what data is available for reporting and SQL queries without reading source code.
